title: Marratooka
summary: Marratooka is a Mattituck placename for a pond and the farm bordering it in Southold town. The history gives Marritook as a related form and treats Marratooka as a later form connected with Mattituck.
map_geometry_source: Approximate modern Marratooka Pond coordinate from USGS/TopoZone-style listing; historical farm boundary not mapped.
history_content: Marratooka is a short cross-reference to Mattituck. It preserves local naming information from C. W. Wickham, proprietor of Marratooka Farm.
translation_content:
The Marratooka entry does not give a separate translation. It points to Mattituck for the fuller placename interpretation. Recorded forms include Marritook and Marratooka.

Why Place Names Matter

“When language is shared by being publicly placed upon a street or site, gifting is an invitation to see from another worldview and honour the pre-existing relationships with the territories on which the street names are placed.”

— Christina Gray and Andrew Ambers, The Rematriation of Indigenous Place Names (2026), Printed p. 18; PDF page 18
whereintheworld_content: This blue marker uses an approximate modern center point for Marratooka Pond in Mattituck. It marks the surviving pond association, not an exact historic farm boundary.
